definitions.explanation: a farming tool with a flat blade on a long handle, used for digging, weeding, and cultivating soil

examples.japanese: {鍬|くわ}で{畑|はたけ}を{耕|たがや}す。
examples.english: To till the field with a hoe.

examples.japanese: {鍬|くわ}を{振|ふ}り{上|あ}げて{土|つち}を{掘|ほ}る。
examples.english: To raise the hoe and dig into the soil.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}は{鍬|くわ}を{使|つか}って{野菜|やさい}を{育|そだ}てている。
examples.english: My grandfather uses a hoe to grow vegetables.

notes:
TRADITIONAL TOOL:
The {鍬|くわ} is one of the most fundamental tools in traditional Japanese agriculture, used for centuries to prepare fields for planting.

USAGE:
- {鍬|くわ}を{入|い}れる (to break ground, start cultivating)
- {鍬|くわ}を{振|ふ}る (to swing a hoe)
- {鍬|くわ}で{耕|たがや}す (to cultivate with a hoe)

TYPES:
- {平鍬|ひらぐわ} (flat hoe)
- {備中鍬|びっちゅうぐわ} (three-pronged hoe)
- {唐鍬|とうぐわ} (heavy digging hoe)

CULTURAL NOTE:
The hoe appears in many Japanese proverbs and expressions related to farming and hard work.

RELATED WORDS:
- {鋤|すき} (plow)
- {農具|のうぐ} (farming tools)
- スコップ (shovel)
- {耕|たがや}す (to cultivate)
